transcript.content: Good [morning/afternoon], I'm Dr. [Name], a psychiatrist. Could you tell me what's been troubling you or what brings you in today?

Good morning. Um... well, I suppose I'm here because I've been having some trouble at home. It's a bit embarrassing, really. I just... I keep arranging my own house around not seeing spiders. 

I put off doing the laundry because it's down in the basement. And I completely avoid the garden shed. I've even started paying people to do small jobs that I know perfectly well how to do myself, just because... well, I just can't make myself go into those spaces.
When you avoid places like the basement or the garden shed, is it mainly because you're afraid of seeing or encountering spiders there?

Yes... it is. 

I mean, I know a spider in the corner of an old house probably isn't going to hurt me. But... the moment I even picture one dropping out of a box, or just sitting near the washer... it just feels enormous. And threatening. 

It's... well, it's embarrassing to admit out loud.
